# Frontend verification on GitHub Actions

Design: not applicable. This workflow changes build infrastructure only.

`workflows/verification.yml` runs on relevant pull requests, pushes to `main` or `codex/ci-validation/**`, and manual dispatch (maintainers can select a nondefault branch). This avoids duplicate branch/PR jobs during normal feature work. The single 30-minute job uses standard `ubuntu-24.04`, Node 24, Temurin Java 21, SDK 36/build-tools 36.0.0 and the repository's Gradle 8.14.3 wrapper. Lint, TypeScript, tests, the `NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_MODE=local` production build, Capacitor sync, debug assembly and APK verification must all succeed before upload. Path filters omit documentation-only changes. Do not configure this path-filtered workflow as an unconditional required check without handling skipped checks. The design studio belongs to the separate team repository and needs its owning-repository checks when affected.

Download the three-day artifact from a successful Actions run: `smart-paper-verification.apk`, `SHA256SUMS`, and `provenance.json`. Run `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` after extracting it. The APK uses `com.aliarefi.smartpaper.verification`, the label **Smart Paper Verification**, and a `-verification` version suffix. Its CI-generated debug certificate differs from the stable signing identity. It installs with separate data alongside stable Smart Paper; it cannot upgrade the stable app, and independent CI runs can have different debug certificates. This is a verification artifact, never a stable release. Device/accessibility QA remains separate. No signing keys or passwords should be provisioned for this workflow.

Use dummy data in this debuggable verification app; it is intended for testing.

Each run generates a fresh verification debug keystore at a fixed `runner.temp` path, explicitly configures debug signing with it, and exports that exact key's public certificate for comparison. It uses public Android debug credentials (`android`/`androiddebugkey`); no stable key or secret is involved. The ephemeral key remains outside the checkout, caches and artifact paths, and is discarded with the hosted runner.

The helpers verify the actual checkout SHA, package ID, source version, debuggable flag, app/launcher labels, APK signature against the runner's debug certificate, and every static web build file against its packaged counterpart. Provenance records the actual checked-out commit (the synthetic merge commit for pull requests), PR head separately, run URL, APK checksum, public certificate digest and tools. These are diagnostic records produced by the checked-out code, not trusted release attestations. The local-data evidence is the explicit build environment plus byte-for-byte packaged output verification, not a device runtime test.

The token has only `contents: read`; checkout does not persist credentials. There are no release-secret references, environments, `pull_request_target`, publishing, tags, commits, or production actions. Helpers reject local signing material and signing environment before Gradle. The CI-only debug manifest and init script leave tracked application/release behavior unchanged. The wrapper archive gets the [official Gradle 8.14.3 checksum](https://services.gradle.org/distributions/gradle-8.14.3-all.zip.sha256) in the ephemeral checkout.

Dependency caches contain only npm package downloads and Gradle caches/wrapper distributions. They exclude node_modules, Android SDK, `.android` debug keys, signing files and outputs. The exact key includes lockfile/Gradle configuration hashes and tool versions; no broad fallback key is used. Only successful default-branch pushes save a cache, and saves over 2 GiB are skipped. PR/manual runs only restore. Obsolete runs on the same event/ref are canceled; artifacts expire after three days. GitHub controls cache eviction; account-wide storage/billing usage must be checked by a maintainer because this workflow does not establish the account quota. Future trusted signing jobs must not reuse verification caches or consume PR artifacts.

Actions are pinned to exact official repository commits (release tag metadata checked on 2026-10-09): [checkout v7.0.1](https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases/tag/v7.0.1), [setup-node v7.1.0](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/releases/tag/v7.1.0), [setup-java v6.0.1](https://github.com/actions/setup-java/releases/tag/v6.0.1), [cache v6.1.0](https://github.com/actions/cache/releases/tag/v6.1.0), and [upload-artifact v7.0.2](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/releases/tag/v7.0.2). Review pins when updating. See [workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax) and [cache boundaries](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching).

## Remote validation

1. On a successful branch push, confirm every named check completes and the artifact includes all three files; download, check SHA256, compare source/run metadata, package/version, and debug signature. A manual rerun confirms exact-key cache restore; main push establishes the default-branch cache.
2. On a temporary `codex/ci-validation/**` branch, add a deliberately failing test. Confirm the Tests step fails, build/upload steps are skipped, and no APK artifact exists. Keep that failure out of main; restore the test with a normal follow-up commit, without rewriting history.
3. Open a fork PR changing relevant source. Confirm read-only permissions, no repository/release secret access, no cache save, PR merge/head metadata and distinct verification ID. Artifact code/metadata from that PR remains untrusted.
4. Push two relevant commits quickly on the same branch and confirm the older run is canceled. Confirm docs-only pushes do not start builds, and artifact retention is three days.
5. In an isolated disposable checkout, exercise helper refusal with dummy signing-file/environment input and verifier failure with an altered packaged asset, package ID or version. Do not inject real signing material.

Remote execution results must be recorded separately; adding YAML does not prove GitHub runner success. Stable signing and the existing team committed-APK publisher are unchanged and remain outside this stage.

## Local fallback

Use the Docker validation prescribed in `AGENTS.md` (Node 24) for `npm ci`, lint, typecheck and `npm test`. Build with `NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_MODE=local npm run build`, then `npx cap sync android` and Java 21/SDK 36 `./gradlew assembleDebug` in `android/`. The ordinary local debug build retains the stable package ID; avoid installing it over stable Smart Paper. The CI isolation helper intentionally refuses local execution. The existing `scripts/build-android-release-docker.sh` remains the stable-signed release fallback under the team release workflow.
